messages:
anya: Heads up — after the kernel-selector rollout last night the streaming tail in us-east-1 shows a jittery p95->p99 hop. Seeing ~30–45ms extra on some streams.

anya: quick repro locally:
```
wrk -t8 -c150 -d30s http://canary/v1/stream?model=redwood-xl -s ./scripts/stream-post.lua
```

mike: digging into profiles now. grabbing `perf` and `pprof` from host-proxy and runtime.

mike: perf top shows lots of writev/sendmsg and syscall overhead in ingress path; user stacks point at framer + preparse.
```
  20.0%  host-proxy  [kernel] writev
  15.5%  host-proc   framer::emit_chunk
  9.7%   host-proc   host-preparse::parse_frame
```

sara: pprof flame from the canary box (60s) — framer and parser dominate; KVCACHE lookup latency increased slightly.
```
pprof samples (600ms total)
framer.coalesce         34% (204ms)
host-preparse.parse    28% (168ms)
kvcache.lookup         12% (72ms)
net-syscalls            6% (36ms)
others                 20% (120ms)
```

tony: context: yesterday's kernel-selector change introduced a preference for the new fast-decoder for >512 token batches. Hypothesis: decoder uses different IO patterns (larger chunk emits) that interact with our streaming framer -> causing more small writev syscalls and fragmentation when clients stream small frames.

tony: also the selector doesn't consider inbound frame sizes or streaming mode — only model/seq_len. That mismatch could push pathological kernel choices for streaming workloads.

anya: metrics: observed KV cache hit-rate down ~1.8% on canary (same traffic), CPU per-token up ~3–5%. p99 increase concentrated in requests with many small frames (<4KB each).

mike: repro experiment: force old decoder kernel -> tail goes away. So selector is very likely the root cause.

mike: short-term mitigations:
- roll back selector on canary (fast but loses perf gains)
- lower max_batch_bytes on canary to avoid crossing kernel threshold
- add host-proxy writev coalescing heuristics for streaming

anya: can we flip max_batch_bytes quickly? that's least risky.

mike: doing it now on canary -> set max_batch_bytes=768KB. watching.

deploy-bot: canary config change 2026-03-21T09:12:05Z -> max_batch_bytes set to 786432 bytes in us-east-1 canary.

infra-bot: alarm: p99-latency-us-east-1 > threshold — investigating correlation with deploy.

sara: adding tracer spans into framer and kvcache lookups; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1299 — contains taggable request ids so we can correlate frame sizes with syscall bursts.

tony: medium-term plan:
- make kernel selector aware of streaming flag and avg inbound frame bytes + client-side windowing
- tune selector thresholds so streaming-heavy traffic stays on stable decoder
- add adaptive coalescing in host-proxy: buffer short frames for up to 500us to combine writev calls when safe

mike: long-term:
- expose a runtime hint from client (streaming vs bulk) and use it in kernel selection
- instrument kvcache to surface hot key sharding and prefetch heuristics

anya: agreed. action items:
- mike: revert selector on canary if max_batch_bytes flip doesn't normalize tail within 30m
- sara: push tracing PR and run a new load job with tagged requests
- tony: run selector sim with mixed seq_len + small-frame distribution and propose new decision rule

mike: metrics look better after max_batch_bytes change — p99 down ~18% in the first 5m. keeping watch for kv hit-rate movement.

anya: thanks all. let's keep this thread as the source of truth for rollback/progress. :thumbsup:
